## Spot a difference of two squares {#difference-of-squares}

Look for the same two terms with a minus sign in one bracket and a plus sign in the other. Use $(a-b)(a+b)=a^2-b^2$.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$(2x-5)(2x+5)$

::: {.fragment}

[Identify the matching terms.]{.annotation}

$a=2x$, $b=5$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Square each term and subtract.]{.annotation}

$=(2x)^2-5^2$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[The FOIL cross products cancel: $10x-10x=0$.]{.annotation}

$=4x^2-25$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$(2x-7)(2x+7)$

Predict which term in the answer will change, then expand on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$=(2x)^2-7^2$

$=4x^2-49$

Only the constant changes.

:::
